Paper Name: Assessing the 3E performance of multiple energy supply scenarios based on photovoltaic, wind turbine, battery and hydrogen systems — Elaouzy et al., 2024, Journal of Energy Storage 99, 113378
NOTES: This paper studies 3 ESSs (grid-connected building in Tangier, Morocco). Paper reports LCOE for 3 scenarios: ESS1 (direct PV+WT supply) = 0.05 $/kWh, ESS2 (with battery storage) = 0.09 $/kWh, ESS3 (with H2 storage) = 0.21 $/kWh. LCOE value used is the baseline ESS1 value. TOTAL ANNUAL LOAD DEMAND not explicitly stated — daily household electrical equipment consumption is 5.57 kWh/day per floor, but annual total not given. LPSP not reported; ECR (Energy Coverage Ratio) used instead: ESS1=52.56%, ESS2=100%, ESS3=100%. COE not reported. rated_PV per panel not explicitly stated — total PV capacity 13.2 kWp across 24 panels (12×2), but individual panel rating not given. Panel dimensions: 2278×1134×35 mm, max efficiency 21.32%. Inverter nominal power 10 kW, max efficiency 97.8%. No diesel generator used. H_min% and H_max% not reported. Per-component O&M and replacement costs not reported — annual OPEX given as 2% of CAPEX (generic). No per-component OPEX/OM breakdown. c_INVT not explicitly stated. Battery costs: 150 $/kWh CAPEX, 10-year lifetime. Heat exchanger: 500 $, 15-year lifetime. Hydrogen storage density: 7.7 kg/m3. Battery capacity: 45 kWh, charging/discharging efficiency: 90%, Li-ion type. Grid sell price assumed at 80% of purchase price. CEF: 0.547 kgCO2e/kWh. Embodied carbon values in Table 4: PV 267.5 kgCO2e/m2, WT 11 gCO2e/kWh, Battery 200 kgCO2e/kWh, H2 1.26 gCO2e/gH2. N_PV (24 panels in 12×2 configuration) but not explicitly labeled as 'number of PV panels' in the context of the N_PV parameter. N_WT appears to be 1 (singular 'a horizontal axis WT') but count not explicitly stated. Per-component replacement costs not reported. A_PV (panel area) derivable from dimensions 2278×1134 mm = ~2.58 m2 but not explicitly stated as area value. Overall system lifetime (T_life) not explicitly stated.
